explorer.repository_tools_tooltip:
Three buttons for fixing data problems.

Restore missing files — checks that everything is in place and brings back anything that is gone. If cloud is set up, it will try to download the missing data from there.

Re-read all files — reads the whole folder again from scratch and brings the file list and history in sync with what is on disk.

Fix version history — repairs the connections between snapshots and file versions. Faster than «Re-read all files».

You do not need these buttons for everyday work — use them only if something looks broken.

help.center_subtitle: Search short guides, see the active storage behavior, and jump straight to the related settings.
help.offline_note: This help is built into the app and works without internet.
help.office_versions_summary: A plain-language overview of what is stored and where to change it.
help.office_versions_p1: When you create or refresh a repository, VeyraFlow records file versions so you can compare and restore them later.
help.office_versions_b1: By default, automatic cleanup is not silently enabled for new repositories.
help.office_versions_b2: If cleanup rules are enabled, older versions may be removed according to age, count or size limits.
help.office_versions_b3: Important snapshots can be protected with archive/protected tags before cleanup runs.
help.office_versions_b4: Default configuration: keep history until you enable cleanup for a repository; global defaults only prepare a template.
help.office_versions_visual: Mini guide: open a repository, select a file, then use Snapshot history to see previous versions and restore options.
help.office_cleanup_summary: Simple rules for space-saving cleanup in Office Mode.
help.office_cleanup_p1: Cleanup is the part of the app that can remove old saved versions to reduce disk usage.
help.office_cleanup_b1: Cleanup can be scheduled or started manually from settings.
help.office_cleanup_b2: Snapshots and file versions covered by active rules can be pruned; current files on disk are not deleted by retention cleanup.
help.office_cleanup_b3: Cloud sync does not make cleanup invisible: cleaned local history is treated as the app's current history state.
help.office_cleanup_callout: Office Mode keeps the controls simpler, but it must still show that cleanup exists and what it can remove.
help.office_cloud_history_summary: What stays in cloud when local cleanup is used.
help.office_cloud_history_p1: Local cleanup and cloud cleanup are separate actions. The safe default is to keep full cloud history even when local history is cleaned.
help.office_cloud_history_b1: Default behavior: local automatic cleanup is off and cloud history is preserved.
help.office_cloud_history_b2: If you clean local history, the cloud copy can still be used as a safer recovery source when cloud history preservation is available.
help.office_cloud_history_b3: Danger actions that make cloud match local history must be confirmed separately and can permanently remove cloud-only history.
help.office_cloud_history_callout: If you are unsure, do not run any action that says it permanently removes cloud history.
help.office_restore_summary: Where to find previous versions and how to recover a file safely.
help.office_restore_p1: To recover a file, open the repository, select the file, then open its snapshot history.
help.office_restore_b1: Restore as copy creates a separate recovered file and does not overwrite the current one.
help.office_restore_b2: Restore with replace overwrites the current file with the selected version.
help.office_restore_b3: If a version was cleaned by retention rules, it may no longer be available for restore.
help.office_restore_visual: Visual path: Repository -> selected file -> Snapshot history -> choose version -> Restore as copy or Restore with replace.
help.pro_retention_summary: Technical behavior of snapshot expiration, pruning and safety guards.
help.pro_retention_p1: Retention Policy controls snapshot expiration, cleanup scheduling and historical version pruning.
help.pro_retention_b1: Rules can target automatic, manual, working or all snapshot triggers.
help.pro_retention_b2: Limits can be based on maximum age, maximum snapshot count and maximum total retained size.
help.pro_retention_b3: Archived snapshots and snapshots carrying protected tags are excluded from cleanup.
help.pro_retention_b4: Use preview/dry-run before applying cleanup when validating new policy values.
help.pro_hierarchy_summary: How effective retention rules are resolved.
help.pro_hierarchy_p1: Effective policy resolution is deterministic and checks the nearest applicable source before falling back.
help.pro_hierarchy_b1: Priority: nested repository override -> repository policy -> parent repository policy -> global policy.
help.pro_hierarchy_b2: A repository with a local override never receives global cleanup rules during global cleanup.
help.pro_hierarchy_b3: A nested repository without local rules inherits the nearest parent repository policy before global policy is considered.
help.pro_hierarchy_visual: Hierarchy diagram: Global defaults at the base, parent repositories above them, nested repositories at the top. The first level with explicit rules wins.
help.pro_cloud_summary: How retention interacts with synced metadata and encrypted block storage.
help.pro_cloud_p1: Retention pruning updates the local history graph and block references. By default, cloud history preservation is treated separately and remains a recovery source.
help.pro_cloud_b1: Current files are not deleted by retention cleanup.
help.pro_cloud_b2: Historical versions removed locally should remain restorable from cloud unless the user explicitly runs a dangerous cloud-prune action.
help.pro_cloud_b3: Encryption and cloud storage diagnostics stay under Sync settings.
help.pro_blocks_title: Orphan block cleanup and dedup safety
help.pro_blocks_summary: Reference-graph rules used before physical block deletion.
help.pro_blocks_p1: Cleanup first removes expired metadata references, then evaluates whether block files are truly orphaned.
help.pro_blocks_b1: A block may be deleted only if no remaining file version, snapshot link, active repository state or retained history entry references it.
help.pro_blocks_b2: Shared and deduplicated blocks are retained while any repository still points at the same block hash.
help.pro_blocks_b3: Cloud synchronization state is treated separately: local block cleanup does not imply cloud history pruning.
help.pro_blocks_callout: This rule prevents data loss when nested repositories or deduplicated files share the same stored block.
help.pro_help_arch_summary: How the built-in documentation is structured for future articles.
help.pro_help_arch_p1: Help pages are defined as data blocks with localized text keys, categories, mode filters and internal navigation links.
help.pro_help_arch_b1: UI rendering is separated from article definitions so new help pages can be added without rebuilding the window layout.
help.pro_help_arch_b2: Blocks support paragraphs, bullets, callouts, settings paths, visual hints and app-internal links.
help.pro_help_arch_b3: The same structure can later load markdown or external article manifests if the documentation grows.
